The design system spec holds records: components, patterns, guidelines, and examples. A component
is a technology-neutral contract (anatomy, parameters, states, rules, tokens), not framework code.
Implement it in whatever technology the project uses.

- Use the `taproot` CLI when you have a terminal, and the `taproot` MCP server when you
  do not. Run the CLI from an installed copy, never an `npx` download per call: in this repository,
  `node packages/spec/bin/taproot.js`; in a project that depends on the package,
  `node_modules/.bin/taproot`.
- Start with `search` to choose a component, then `get` it and follow its links: `alternative` for
  when it is the wrong choice, `follows` for the patterns and guidelines it applies, `examples` for
  worked usage.
- Use `rules` to review work, and cite each rule by its address (for example
  `component.button#label-describes-result`) with its level (MUST, SHOULD, MAY). A component's
  rules include those of the patterns and guidelines it follows, at their own addresses (for
  example `pattern.form-field#error-blocks-submit`).
- Use `tokens` for the design tokens a component part uses in a variant or state. Add `--resolve`
  (MCP: `resolve`) for values. Use `format` for what records do not repeat: the system-wide
  constants, such as border width and focus-ring width and offset, with their tokens.
- Before writing code, `get` the component with the implementation for your technology:
  `--impl web` for web components, `--impl react` for React (MCP: `implementation`). It gives the
  package, what to import, and the attribute or prop that implements each parameter. Never derive
  those names from parameter names. Once per project, read `setup --impl <name>` (MCP: `setup`)
  for what every component shares: installing the package, loading its styles, and fonts.
- Components style only themselves. Before building a page, `get guideline.page-setup` for the
  page's base font, text color, background, and heading recipes, and load the base stylesheet it
  names when your technology has one.
- For several lookups, run them in one `batch` with the CLI (for example
  `taproot batch --command "get button --impl web" --command "tokens button"`), or make the
  tool calls in parallel on the MCP server.

$ taproot setup --impl web
# Web components setup

What every web component needs, once per project. Each component's own file in this folder maps its
API; `taproot setup --impl web` prints this one.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @taproot-ds/web-components @taproot-ds/tokens
```

## Load the styles

Load the token stylesheet once, at the application root, before any component renders. Without it,
the components have no colors, spacing, or type. The optional base stylesheet styles the page
around them: the base font, text color, background, and a type recipe for each heading level
(`guideline.page-setup`). The components style only themselves.

```js
import "@taproot-ds/tokens/css";
import "@taproot-ds/tokens/base"; // optional page defaults
```

Without a bundler, link the files from the tokens package instead:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/node_modules/@taproot-ds/tokens/dist/css/tokens.css" />
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/node_modules/@taproot-ds/tokens/dist/css/base.css" />
```

The components read semantic tokens directly, so they follow the active theme. With no
`data-theme` on the root element, the theme follows the system preference; `data-theme="light"` or
`"dark"` overrides it. The tokens a component reads are not a customization API.

## Fonts

The font tokens name Lora, Source Sans 3, and JetBrains Mono, with system fallbacks. The packages do
not ship the font files. The tokens package's readme has the links to load them.

## Register the elements

Import the package root once to register every element under its `ds-` tag:

```js
import "@taproot-ds/web-components";
```

Or import one component's module and call its define function, as each component's Import section
shows. A define function takes another tag name when `ds-` names collide.

The modules are standard ES modules with no runtime dependencies. Without a bundler, map the bare
package names with an import map, or import the files under `node_modules/@taproot-ds/web-components/src/`.

$ taproot get guideline.page-setup
# Page setup

Set the page's base font, text color, background, and heading type from semantic tokens, because components style only themselves.

The components style only themselves. The page around them, the text between them, and the
headings above them get no style from any component. Without these defaults, components look right
while the page around them falls back to the platform's serif font and plain white, and nothing
reports the gap.

## What the page sets

| Page element | Token | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Background | `semantic.color.background.default` | The page itself. Raised areas use `semantic.color.background.surface`. |
| Base text | `semantic.typography.body.md` | Font family, size, weight, line height, and letter spacing. |
| Text color | `semantic.color.foreground.default` | Supporting text uses `semantic.color.foreground.muted`. |
| Small print | `semantic.typography.body.sm` | Captions and fine print. |
| Page title (level 1) | `semantic.typography.heading.lg` | One per page. |
| Section heading (level 2) | `semantic.typography.heading.md` | |
| Subsection heading (level 3) | `semantic.typography.heading.sm` | The recipe Card uses for its title. |
| Deeper headings (levels 4 to 6) | `semantic.typography.title` | The bold sans title Alert and Dialog use. |
| Code | `semantic.typography.code.md` | Inline code and code blocks. |
| Eyebrow above a heading | `semantic.typography.eyebrow` | A short category line, not a heading. |

A typography token such as `semantic.typography.body.md` is a recipe: it groups a font family,
size, weight, line height, and letter spacing, and each is its own token
(`semantic.typography.body.md.fontFamily`). Set all five together. Mixing parts of two recipes
produces a size and line height that were never designed together.

For the values in each theme, read the token package, or resolve a component that uses the
recipe, such as `taproot tokens card --part title --resolve`.

## Token names in your technology

A token reference such as `semantic.typography.body.md.fontFamily` is technology-neutral. Each
technology's token package publishes it under its own name, and that package says how. In the web
package, a reference becomes a CSS custom property: prefix `--ds-`, join the segments with hyphens,
and turn camel case into hyphenated words, so the reference above is
`--ds-semantic-typography-body-md-font-family`. Check a name against the package's stylesheet
before you rely on it (`no-guessed-names`).

## Fonts

The font tokens name the system's typefaces with fallbacks. The token package does not ship the
font files. Load the typefaces the way your platform does, before the page renders; the token
package's readme lists them and gives the web links to load them. Without them, the fallbacks keep the page readable but it does not
look like the system.

## Theme

The token package follows the reader's light or dark preference, and lets the page choose one
instead. Set the theme at the root of the page so the background, the base text, and every
component change together. A part of the page that sets its own colors without semantic tokens
does not change with them.

## Spacing and layout

Lay out the page with the spacing primitives, `primitives.space.*`, and put product layout
between components rather than inside them (`guideline.compose-or-propose`). The system has no
grid, container, or page template component; compose those in product code.

## Rules

### Behavior

- **MUST** load-tokens: Load the token package once, at the root of the page, before any component renders. Without it, components have no colors, spacing, or type.
- **MUST** page-base-text: The page's base text uses the body recipe, `semantic.typography.body.md`, in `semantic.color.foreground.default`. Text the components do not draw would otherwise fall back to the platform's default font and color.
- **MUST** page-background: The page background is `semantic.color.background.default`, so it follows the active theme with the components on it.
- **SHOULD** heading-recipes: Each heading level uses a heading recipe: the page title `semantic.typography.heading.lg`, section headings `semantic.typography.heading.md`, subsection headings `semantic.typography.heading.sm`, and deeper levels `semantic.typography.title`. Choose the level by the document outline, and the recipe by the level.
- **SHOULD** base-stylesheet: Where the token package offers a base stylesheet for your technology, load it rather than writing the page defaults by hand. It applies these rules with names that are already right. `taproot setup --impl <name>` names it for each implementation.
- **MUST** no-guessed-names: Take each token's name in your technology from the token package or a lookup, never from a guess. A misspelled token name fails silently and the platform default shows instead.

## Links

### related

- [Accessibility](guideline.accessibility)
- [Compose or propose](guideline.compose-or-propose)

$ taproot get switch --impl web
# Switch

Use Switch to turn a setting on or off and apply the change immediately.

A two-state setting with a visible label and optional hint or error. Changing it applies the setting immediately.

## When to use

- Turn a setting on or off without a separate submit action.

## When not to use

- Record an independent choice for later submission. Use [Checkbox](component.checkbox) instead. Checkbox communicates a choice that takes effect on submit.
- Choose one item from a list. Use [Radio group](component.radio-group) instead. A switch represents one independent setting.

## Anatomy

| Part | Role | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| field | container | Setting and its supporting messages. |
| choice | container | Track and label side by side. |
| control | interactive-surface | Track that toggles the setting. |
| indicator | indicator | Thumb position communicates on or off without color alone. |
| label | label | Visible setting name. |
| hint | description | Optional consequence or guidance. |
| error | description | Optional failure message. |

## Parameters

| Name | Kind | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | string |  |  | Visible accessible name that stays the same in both states. |
| hint | string |  |  | Supporting guidance associated with the setting. |
| error | string |  |  | Failure text that marks the setting invalid. |
| checked | boolean |  | `false` | Whether the setting is on. |
| disabled | boolean |  | `false` | Prevents interaction and removes the setting from keyboard navigation. |
| name | string |  |  | Optional form field name. The value is recorded under this name when on. |
| value | string |  |  | Value recorded when on. Defaults to on. |

## Events

- `input`: The user changed the setting.
- `change`: The user committed the setting change. Apply the setting in response.

## States

`default`, `hover`, `focus`, `checked`, `disabled`, `invalid`

## Rules

Includes the rules of pattern.form-field, guideline.accessibility, which this component follows. Cite each rule by the address shown.

### Content

- **MUST** stable-visible-label: Provide a visible positive setting name that does not change between on and off.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#visible-label: Provide a visible label that names the value. Placeholder text is not a label.
  - Do: Email address
  - Avoid: Enter email
- **SHOULD** pattern.form-field#hint-adds-information: Use a hint only for format, purpose, or consequence that the label does not already state.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#error-says-what-to-fix: Write the error as what to fix.
  - Do: Enter an email address with an @ sign
  - Avoid: Invalid
- **SHOULD** pattern.form-field#explain-disabled: When the reason a control is unavailable is not obvious, explain it nearby.

### Behavior

- **MUST** immediate-effect: Apply the setting immediately after interaction. If saving fails restore the prior state and explain the failure.
- **MUST** toggle-on-activate: Activating the track or label or pressing Space toggles checked and reports input then change.
- **MUST** programmatic-no-events: Programmatic state changes do not report user input or change.
- **SHOULD** form-value: The value submits only while the switch is on. Reset restores the initial state.
  - Extends: pattern.form-field#form-value
  - Applies when: The control belongs to a form.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#error-marks-invalid: A non-empty error marks the control invalid, and clearing the error removes that state.
- **SHOULD** pattern.form-field#clear-error: Clear the error when the person edits the value, and on form reset, which restores the value but leaves the error.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#error-blocks-submit: While a non-empty error is set, the control blocks its form from submitting.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#disabled-prevents-interaction: Disabled prevents interaction from pointer and keyboard.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#disabled-submits-nothing: A disabled control submits nothing.
- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#not-a-control: The component is not focusable and does not activate.
  - Applies when: The component is not interactive.

### Accessibility

- **MUST** not-color-alone: Thumb position communicates the state without color alone.
  - Extends: guideline.accessibility#not-color-alone
- **MUST** forced-colors: Keep the track outline and thumb and keyboard focus visible under forced colors.
  - Extends: guideline.accessibility#forced-colors
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#label-is-name: The visible label is the control's accessible name.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#described-by-hint-and-error: The hint and the error are associated with the control, so assistive technology reads them as its description.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#invalid-not-color-alone: The invalid state always includes the error text, so meaning never depends on color alone.
- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#visible-focus: Keyboard focus is visibly indicated on every focusable part, in every variant and state.
  - Applies when: A part of the component takes keyboard focus.

### Waived

- pattern.form-field#required-blocks-submit: A switch applies its setting immediately and is always on or off, so it has no required option.
- pattern.form-field#required-announced: A switch applies its setting immediately and is always on or off, so it has no required option.

## Accessibility

- Role: Switch
- Name: From the visible label.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Move focus to or from the switch. |
| Space | Toggle the setting. |

## Rationale

- **One size with no density or icon-only variant.** The track and thumb sizes are in the token map. The thumb is centered across the track, and at each end it sits as far from the end as from the top and bottom. Surrounding layout controls density. Sizes are spacing primitives because no semantic size role exists (tokens ADR 0003), so the track is 32 by 20 rather than the earlier 32 by 18, which no primitive expresses.
- **No mixed state or required setting or loading state.** A setting is on or off. The consumer can disable it during saving and restore its previous state with an error if saving fails.
- **No animation or reduced motion variation.** The thumb changes position immediately.
- **The thumb follows the inline direction in right-to-left layouts.** Off sits at the start and on sits at the end of the track.
- **Consume existing semantic colors and typography with the semantic pill radius.** The track and thumb need circular ends. The pill radius expresses circular ends.
- **Disabled colors override checked and invalid colors while thumb position remains visible.** Availability and the current setting must both be communicated.
- **No visited state and spacing consumes existing primitives.** Selection does not track navigation history. The system has no semantic spacing roles for choice rows.
- **Checked and invalid borders take precedence over hover.** Hover strengthens only the unchecked valid control. Checked and invalid together retain the checked background with the danger border.

## Links

### alternative

- [Checkbox](component.checkbox) — Record an independent choice for later submission. Checkbox communicates a choice that takes effect on submit.
- [Radio group](component.radio-group) — Choose one item from a list. A switch represents one independent setting.

### alternative-to

- [Checkbox](component.checkbox) — Apply a setting as soon as it is toggled, with no submit. A checkbox value takes effect when its form is submitted.
- [Slider](component.slider) — Turn a single setting on or off. Two states are a toggle, not a range.

### follows

- [Accessibility](guideline.accessibility)
- [Compose or propose](guideline.compose-or-propose)
- [Form field](pattern.form-field)

### related

- [Checkbox](component.checkbox)

## Web implementation

- Package: `@taproot-ds/web-components`
- Element: `<ds-switch>`

### Import

```js
import { defineSwitch } from "@taproot-ds/web-components/switch";

defineSwitch();
```

### Usage

```html
<ds-switch label="Send desktop notifications" hint="Changes apply immediately." checked></ds-switch>
```

### API

| Name | Kind | Implements | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | attribute | parameter `label` | string | Visible accessible name that stays the same in both states. |
| `hint` | attribute | parameter `hint` | string | Supporting guidance associated with the setting. |
| `error` | attribute | parameter `error` | string | Failure text that marks the setting invalid. |
| `checked` | attribute | parameter `checked` | boolean | Whether the setting is on. |
| `name` | attribute | parameter `name` | string | Optional form field name. The value is recorded under this name when on. |
| `value` | attribute | parameter `value` | string | Value recorded when on. Defaults to on. |
| `disabled` | attribute | parameter `disabled` | boolean | Prevents interaction and removes the setting from keyboard navigation. |
| `form` | property |  | `HTMLFormElement \| null` | The associated form, including association across the shadow boundary. |
| `input` | event | event `input` |  | The user changed the setting. |
| `change` | event | event `change` |  | The user committed the setting change. Apply the setting in response. |

A row with no Implements entry is specific to this implementation, not part of the spec.

Listen for `change` and apply the setting immediately. Read the live `checked` property.
If saving fails, restore the previous `checked` value and set `error` to explain the failure.
The `checked` attribute is the initial state; form reset restores it.

Tokens: 38 bindings, left out here. Run `taproot tokens component.switch` to filter them by part, condition, or property.
Setup: install, styles, and fonts are the same for every component. Run `taproot setup --impl web` once per project.


$ taproot get slider --impl web
# Slider

Use Slider to choose one number from a continuous range when the approximate value matters more than the exact one.

A track between a minimum and a maximum with a thumb that marks the chosen value. People drag the thumb or step it with the keyboard, and the current value is shown beside the label.

## When to use

- Set a level where people judge by feel and see the effect, such as volume or brightness.
- Narrow a range filter to an approximate amount, such as a maximum price.

## When not to use

- Enter an exact number, or a number from a very large range. Use [Text field](component.text-field) instead. Typing is faster and more precise than dragging to one value among hundreds.
- Choose from a few named options, such as Small, Medium, and Large. Use [Select](component.select) instead. Named options are choices, not points on a scale. A select names each one.
- Show progress or a measured amount people cannot change. Use [Progress bar](component.progress-bar) instead. A slider is a control. A bar that only reports a value must not look adjustable.
- Turn a single setting on or off. Use [Switch](component.switch) instead. Two states are a toggle, not a range.

## Anatomy

| Part | Role | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| field | container | Header, track, hint, and error stacked together. |
| header | container | Label and value on one line. |
| label | label | Visible name for the value. |
| value | description | The current value as text, at the end of the header. |
| track | container | The line from the minimum to the maximum. |
| fill | indicator | The part of the track from the minimum to the thumb. |
| thumb | interactive-surface | The handle people drag or step to change the value. |
| hint | description | Optional supporting guidance. |
| error | description | Optional message that says what to fix. |

## Parameters

| Name | Kind | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | string |  |  | Visible label. This is the accessible name. |
| hint | string |  |  | Supporting guidance. Included in the accessible description when set. |
| error | string |  |  | What to fix. A non-empty value marks the slider invalid and is included in the accessible description. |
| value | number |  |  | Current value. The value given at creation is the initial value that reset restores. Defaults to min. |
| min | number |  | `0` | Smallest value, at the start of the track. |
| max | number |  | `100` | Largest value, at the end of the track. Greater than min. |
| step | number |  | `1` | Distance between the values people can choose, counted from min. The value is always min plus a whole number of steps. |
| name | string |  |  | Form field name. The value is submitted under this name. |
| disabled | boolean |  | `false` | Prevents changing the value. A disabled slider does not submit its value. |

## Events

- `input`: The value changed while a person drags the thumb or presses a key. Reported for every new value.
- `change`: A person finished changing the value: released the thumb or the key. Reported once, and only when the value differs from the value before they started.

## States

`default`, `hover`, `focus`, `dragging`, `disabled`, `invalid`

## Rules

Includes the rules of pattern.form-field, guideline.accessibility, which this component follows. Cite each rule by the address shown.

### Content

- **MUST** visible-label: Provide a visible label that names what the value sets, such as Volume.
  - Extends: pattern.form-field#visible-label
- **MUST** value-shown: Show the current value as text beside the label, and give assistive technology the same text. Position on the track alone does not say the value.
- **SHOULD** pattern.form-field#hint-adds-information: Use a hint only for format, purpose, or consequence that the label does not already state.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#error-says-what-to-fix: Write the error as what to fix.
  - Do: Enter an email address with an @ sign
  - Avoid: Invalid
- **SHOULD** pattern.form-field#explain-disabled: When the reason a control is unavailable is not obvious, explain it nearby.

### Behavior

- **MUST** value-in-range: The value is always between min and max and lands on a step. A value given outside the range moves to the nearest end, and a value between steps moves to the nearest step.
- **MUST** drag-or-press: Dragging the thumb or pressing anywhere on the track moves the value to that point and reports input for each new value.
- **MUST** keyboard-steps: Arrow keys move the value by one step, Page Up and Page Down by a tenth of the range rounded to a step, and Home and End to min and max. Each key press reports input then change.
- **MUST** change-on-release: Report change once when a person releases the thumb or the key, and only when the value differs from the value before they started. Apply costly work, such as a new search, on change rather than input.
- **MUST** programmatic-no-events: Setting the value from outside, or a form reset, does not report input or change.
- **SHOULD** form-value: The current number submits under the name, and reset restores the initial value.
  - Extends: pattern.form-field#form-value
  - Applies when: The control belongs to a form.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#error-marks-invalid: A non-empty error marks the control invalid, and clearing the error removes that state.
- **SHOULD** pattern.form-field#clear-error: Clear the error when the person edits the value, and on form reset, which restores the value but leaves the error.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#error-blocks-submit: While a non-empty error is set, the control blocks its form from submitting.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#disabled-prevents-interaction: Disabled prevents interaction from pointer and keyboard.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#disabled-submits-nothing: A disabled control submits nothing.
- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#not-a-control: The component is not focusable and does not activate.
  - Applies when: The component is not interactive.

### Accessibility

- **MUST** thumb-contrast: The thumb and fill are visible against the track and the surface around it, so position is readable without the value text.
- **MUST** forced-colors: Keep the track outline, the fill, the thumb, and keyboard focus visible under forced colors.
  - Extends: guideline.accessibility#forced-colors
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#label-is-name: The visible label is the control's accessible name.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#described-by-hint-and-error: The hint and the error are associated with the control, so assistive technology reads them as its description.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#invalid-not-color-alone: The invalid state always includes the error text, so meaning never depends on color alone.
- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#visible-focus: Keyboard focus is visibly indicated on every focusable part, in every variant and state.
  - Applies when: A part of the component takes keyboard focus.
- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#not-color-alone: Meaning never depends on color alone. Text, shape, or position carries it too.

### Waived

- pattern.form-field#required-blocks-submit: A slider always has a value between min and max, so it cannot be required.
- pattern.form-field#required-announced: A slider always has a value between min and max, so it cannot be required.

## Accessibility

- Role: Slider
- Name: From the visible label.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Move focus to or from the thumb. |
| Arrow Right / Arrow Up | Increase the value by one step. |
| Arrow Left / Arrow Down | Decrease the value by one step. |
| Page Up / Page Down | Increase or decrease by a tenth of the range. |
| Home / End | Move to min or max. |

## Rationale

- **One thumb, horizontal, with no tick marks.** The uses in the usage section need one value along the reading direction. A two-thumb range, a vertical slider, and tick marks can be added when a layout needs them.
- **The value text is the number in the reader's locale. There is no format parameter.** Units go in the label, such as "Volume (%)" or "Maximum price (USD)". A format parameter for units or currency can be added when several uses need the same one.
- **The value text is not editable.** A slider is for approximate values. When people need an exact number, use Text field, as the usage section says.
- **No required state.** A slider always has a value, so it can never be empty.
- **Disabled removes the thumb from keyboard navigation and greys every part.** Nothing can change while disabled, so focus would only be a stop with nothing to do. The value text stays readable so people still see the setting.
- **An error recolors the fill and thumb and always shows its message.** A value can be wrong for reasons outside the slider, such as a budget above an account limit. The message carries the meaning, so the danger color is never the only signal.
- **No selected, checked, or loading state.** A slider holds a number, not an on or off state. Work that follows a change belongs to the page, which can disable the slider while it waits.
- **One size, filling the width of its container.** The track length comes from the layout. The thumb is large enough to grab with a pointer. Sizes are spacing primitives because no semantic size role exists (tokens ADR 0003).
- **The label is visible and required. There is no label-free slider.** Position on a track does not say what it sets, for sighted people either.
- **The track runs in the reading direction, so it mirrors in right-to-left layouts.** Min sits at the start and max at the end. Arrow keys follow the visual direction.
- **Nothing animates. The thumb and fill move with the value.** Motion would lag behind the pointer while dragging.
- **In forced colors the track draws an outline, and the fill and thumb use a system color.** Forced colors drop background colors, which would leave an invisible track. An outlined track with a solid fill and thumb keeps the position visible.
- **The fill and thumb use the primary action color, not the brand color Progress bar uses.** A slider is a control, and action colors say it can be changed. Progress bar uses brand color because it cannot.
- **The invalid fill and thumb use the danger status border color.** The danger status background is a pale tint meant to sit behind text, so a fill and thumb in it disappear against the track. The danger border color is strong in both themes, and Switch uses it for its invalid state too.
- **The disabled fill and thumb use the disabled border color.** No color token covers a disabled filled part. The disabled border color is visible against the disabled track and reads as unavailable, so a new token for one component is not needed.
- **The thumb border uses the surface color.** A ring in the surface color separates the thumb from the fill behind it, so the thumb edge stays visible where the two share a color.

## Links

### alternative

- [Progress bar](component.progress-bar) — Show progress or a measured amount people cannot change. A slider is a control. A bar that only reports a value must not look adjustable.
- [Select](component.select) — Choose from a few named options, such as Small, Medium, and Large. Named options are choices, not points on a scale. A select names each one.
- [Switch](component.switch) — Turn a single setting on or off. Two states are a toggle, not a range.
- [Text field](component.text-field) — Enter an exact number, or a number from a very large range. Typing is faster and more precise than dragging to one value among hundreds.

## Web implementation

- Package: `@taproot-ds/web-components`
- Element: `<ds-slider>`

### Import

```js
import { defineSlider } from "@taproot-ds/web-components/slider";

defineSlider();
```

### Usage

```html
<ds-slider
  label="Maximum price (USD)"
  hint="Shows homes at or below this price."
  name="max-price"
  max="2000"
  step="50"
  value="800"
></ds-slider>
```

### API

| Name | Kind | Implements | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | attribute | parameter `label` | string | Visible label. This is the accessible name. |
| `hint` | attribute | parameter `hint` | string | Supporting guidance. Included in the accessible description when set. |
| `error` | attribute | parameter `error` | string | What to fix. A non-empty value marks the slider invalid and is included in the accessible description. |
| `value` | attribute | parameter `value` | number | Current value. The value given at creation is the initial value that reset restores. Defaults to min. |
| `min` | attribute | parameter `min` | number | Smallest value, at the start of the track. |
| `max` | attribute | parameter `max` | number | Largest value, at the end of the track. Greater than min. |
| `step` | attribute | parameter `step` | number | Distance between the values people can choose, counted from min. The value is always min plus a whole number of steps. |
| `name` | attribute | parameter `name` | string | Form field name. The value is submitted under this name. |
| `disabled` | attribute | parameter `disabled` | boolean | Prevents changing the value. A disabled slider does not submit its value. |
| `form` | property |  | `HTMLFormElement \| null` | The associated form, including association across the shadow boundary. |
| `input` | event | event `input` |  | The value changed while a person drags the thumb or presses a key. Reported for every new value. |
| `change` | event | event `change` |  | A person finished changing the value: released the thumb or the key. Reported once, and only when the value differs from the value before they started. |

A row with no Implements entry is specific to this implementation, not part of the spec.

### Value

The `value` attribute sets the initial value, and form reset restores it. The `value` property is
the current number. Setting it changes the current value and fires no events
(`component.slider#programmatic-no-events`). Without a `value` attribute the slider starts at
`min`. A value outside the range or between steps reads back as the nearest allowed value.

### Input and change

`input` fires for every new value while a person drags or presses a key, and `change` fires once
when they release (`component.slider#change-on-release`). Read `event.target.value` in either. Run
costly work, such as a new search, from `change`.

### Forms

With `name`, the value submits as a number string. To validate in your own code, set `novalidate`
on the form so the submit reaches your listener, and set `error` on a slider that needs a
correction. Clear `error` on its `change` event and when the form resets, because a reset leaves it
set.

### Value text

The value beside the label is the number formatted for the `lang` of the nearest ancestor that has
one, or the browser's locale. Put units in the label.

### Reading direction

The track follows the element's CSS `direction`: with `dir="rtl"` on the slider or an ancestor,
`min` is on the right and Arrow Right decreases the value.
